stages.rule: Required systems/mission determine departments; organization doctrine names them.
Bridge/control, engineering, medical/security/sensor coverage are sized from actual design and readiness.
Research, maintenance, administration, education/services and project staff are mission/capability dependent.
Minimum safe != target operational != maximum berthing.
Use operator/class guidance, crew size, fatigue, mission tempo and command policy.
Assign primary watch shares and reserve/relief without hiding vacancies.
Each slot has qualification, rank/grade if any, duty station, redundancy and watch requirements.
Use existing eligible characters first where context provides them; generate persistent people only for real slots.
Duty + handoff + obligations + protected rest + meals + free time; no overlaps.
Use personality/preferences/culture plus actual ship facilities; do not force activity.
Flag vacancies, fatigue risk, overwork, unsupported services and qualification gaps.

normal_operation_rules: Every person receives one primary schedule identity but may have secondary/acting roles.
Department heads need not stand every bridge/department watch personally.
Commanding officer is not assumed to remain on bridge for an entire shipboard day.
Small-crew ships may use staggered sleep/on-call instead of symmetric watch teams.
High-tempo missions may temporarily use double shifts but create fatigue debt.
